title: Dedicated onboarding flow for throughput guarantees and fleet guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customer onboarding for Dedicated capacity is inconsistent between sales, solutions, and infra teams. Current reservation requests often omit critical workload profiles (burst patterns, latency SLOs, KV cache reuse expectations) which results in conservative capacity commitments or surprise throttling. Goal: Deliver an operational onboarding flow and runbook that (1) captures workload-level throughput guarantees and burst envelopes, (2) maps those to fleet allocation and autoscaling guardrails, and (3) provides a predictable approval path with clear knobs for trade-offs (latency vs cost). This ticket scopes the PM-owned flow, acceptance criteria, and handoffs to Eng and Solutions.
acceptance_criteria: A single onboarding form (spreadsheet + web intake) captures throughput targets, 95th/99th latency SLOs, burst duration, typical sequence length distribution, and KV cache locality requirements.

A documented mapping table that translates workload profiles into recommended fleet profiles: min/max vGPU count, preferred region tiers, autoscale policy template (scale step, cooldown, buffer), and suggested quantization profiles.
Playbook for approvals that includes explicit risk tiers (low/medium/high) and associated SLAs for procurement, security review, and deployment windows.
Two operational templates (Standard and High-Burst) added to the provisioning UI and console: selecting a template prepopulates autoscale and routing guardrails.
Handoff checklist and a documented runbook for SRE/Oncall with rollback steps and fallback model variants for graceful degradation.
Stakeholders (Solutions, Sales, Eng runtime, SRE, Security) have reviewed and provided sign-off in the doc and via the approval thread.
steps: Draft intake form fields with Solutions and runtime Eng (include sample payloads and traffic patterns).
Prototype mapping table: run 3 sample workloads through cost/latency simulator to validate recommendations.
Create two autoscale policy templates (steady-state and burst-capable) and define default buffer percentages and cooldowns.
Design approval workflow: automatic checks (quota, KMS attachments), manual gates (security/compliance), and SLA timers for procurement.
Add provisioning template artifacts to Console repo and link UI feature request for engineering implementation.
Run a pilot with one enterprise customer, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then iterate on thresholds and documentation.
decisions: Use a two-template approach (Standard, High-Burst) instead of fully bespoke allocations to reduce approval friction.
Autoscale policies will expose three knobs to customers: target buffer (%), max burst multiple, and cooldown seconds. Default values will be opinionated and adjustable by Dedicated admins.
Throughput guarantees will be expressed as committed RPS and a burst envelope (RPS for up to X minutes) rather than raw GPU counts to keep commitments customer-centric.
